newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end 2.08 pct up as key stocks rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end 2.08 pct up as key stocks rebound.

text.p: A slate of large capitalised stocks rebounded in moderate-volume trading to bring the key market index to finish 2.08 percent higher, dealers said.
The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's key Composite Index rose 23.02 points to end at 1,127.60.
The Dow Jones Industrials rose 44.95 points to 6,703.55 on Friday.
"I think the market probably needs time to consolidate. Otherwise any rebound cannot be sustained," said an equity salesman at Jardine Fleming.
Telecommunications stock Telekom and power concern Tenaga Nasional each rose 40 cents to 12.00 and 17.90 ringgit, to boost the Composite Index.
Other strong heavyweights include Maybank's 50-cent gain to 27.00, Sime Darby's 15-cent rise to 8.25, and the 50-cent gain of Petronas Gas to 8.55.
The moderate volume suggested that sentiment remained quite fragile after the recent sharp slides, dealers said.
At the close, market volume stood at 298 million shares, valued at 1.89 billion ringgit. Gainers led losers 614 to 73.
"Volume is still moderate, not aggressive. The market will test 1,150 again but it will take time to break that," said a dealer at a bank-owned brokerage.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot April contract rose 20.2 points to close at 1,124.5 on volume of 767 lots, while the May futures contract was up 16.5 points to 1,122.5 with 36 lots traded.
